newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland mulls support to Gulf of Bothnia ferries.
newsitem.headline: Finland mulls support to Gulf of Bothnia ferries.

text.p: Finland and Sweden should make sure that ferry traffic in the Gulf of Bothnia is supported either by national aid or by allowing duty-free sales on board, a Finnish transport ministry committee said on Tuesday.

It said year-round traffic across the Gulf was important for business, culture and social life on both sides of the central Gulf of Bothnia -- around Vaasa in Finland and Umea in Sweden -- and should be kept alive.
Duty-free sales are due to end on July 1, 1999, and if Finland cannot reach agreement with the EU to allow those sales to continue Finland and Sweden should pay direct aid, it said. @

"According to the preliminary calculations the committee has used, year-round traffic would require subsidies to an amount of about 30 million markka with the current ships -- including vessel capital costs," the committee said in a report.

It said Finnish Silja's Silja Line was operating year-round traffic on the route between Vaasa and Umea and that there was summer-time traffic between Pietarsaari in Finland and Skelleftea and Umea in Sweden.
But the best solution would be to allow continued duty-free sales after 1999, it said.

In 1996, 865,000 passengers and about 8,000 freight units were transported across the middle of the Gulf of Bothnia, and preliminary data shows that 70 percent of passengers were Finns and almost 30 percent Swedes, it said.
Other nationalities were a marginal group, it added.
